case.title: COPD flare, respiratory failure considered and excluded
case.summary: A man with a COPD flare was briefly flagged in the ER for possible respiratory failure, but the admitting doctor examined him and documented that he did not have it.

documents.author: T. Achebe, MD (Radiology)
documents.text:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, portable AP
INDICATION: Dyspnea, wheezing.
FINDINGS: Hyperinflated lungs with flattened hemidiaphragms. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
IMPRESSION: Hyperinflation consistent with COPD. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

documents.author: D. Ferreira, MD (Emergency Medicine)
documents.text:
CC: Shortness of breath, wheezing.

HPI: 69M with COPD, current smoker, presents with 3 days of worsening SOB, wheeze and increased sputum, now yellow. Using albuterol q2h at home without relief. No fever, chest pain or leg swelling. Not on home O2.

Vitals: T 37.3, HR 108, BP 148/90, RR 26, SpO2 87% RA on arrival.
Exam: Tripoding on arrival, diffuse expiratory wheezes, prolonged expiration, mild accessory muscle use.

Labs: WBC 10.8, Hgb 15.9, BMP unremarkable. Troponin <0.01.
CXR: hyperinflation, no infiltrate or effusion.

Course: DuoNeb x3, methylprednisolone 125 mg IV, azithromycin 500 mg. On 2 L NC SpO2 93%; RR 22.

Assessment/Plan:
1. COPD exacerbation.
2. Acute hypoxic respiratory failure? ABG pending.
Dispo: Admit to medicine.

documents.author: K. Whitaker, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL

HPI: See ED. Feels much better after nebs. Two exacerbations in the past year treated as outpatient.

PMH: COPD (FEV1 52% predicted, 2025). HTN. HLD. Depression.
Meds: fluticasone/vilanterol 200/25 1 inh daily, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol PRN, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily.
Social: Smokes 1 ppd cigarettes, 45 pack-years. Retired roofer.

Exam: T 37.0, HR 94, BP 136/82, RR 20, SpO2 92% on room air at rest. Speaking full sentences, no accessory muscle use, scattered expiratory wheezes, fair air movement.
ABG (RA, 08:40): pH 7.39 / pCO2 45 / pO2 66 / HCO3 27.

Assessment/Plan:
1. COPD with acute exacerbation - prednisone 40 mg daily x5 days, DuoNeb q4h + albuterol q2h PRN, azithromycin x3 days. Titrate O2 to SpO2 88-92% only if needed.
   Not in respiratory failure: SpO2 92% RA, no increased work of breathing, ABG without hypoxemia or hypercapnia requiring support.
2. Tobacco use - cigarette dependence; nicotine patch 21 mg, cessation counseling >3 min.
3. HTN - continue amlodipine.
4. HLD - atorvastatin.
5. Depression - stable on sertraline.
VTE ppx: enoxaparin.

documents.author: R. Delgado, RN
documents.text: Arrived to unit on 2 L NC. Per order weaned to room air at 11:00; SpO2 92-93% RA at rest, RR 20, speaking in full sentences, no accessory muscle use. DuoNeb given at 10:00 and 14:00 per RT. Pt requesting to go outside to smoke; nicotine patch applied, smoking cessation pamphlet given. Steady gait, independent in room.

documents.author: K. Whitaker, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HOSPITAL DAY 3

S: Breathing near baseline, walked hallway without stopping.
O: HR 84, RR 18, SpO2 93% RA, ambulatory SpO2 90% RA. Faint end-expiratory wheeze.

Assessment/Plan:
1. COPD exacerbation - improving. Space DuoNeb to q6h. Prednisone day 3/5. No home O2 need on ambulatory testing.
2. Tobacco dependence - on patch, wants to try varenicline.
3. HTN, HLD, depression - stable.

documents.author: K. Whitaker, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit: 09/16/2026   Discharge: 09/19/2026   Disposition: Home

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. COPD with acute exacerbation
2. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes
3. Hypertension
4. Hyperlipidemia
5. Depression

HOSPITAL COURSE: Admitted with COPD exacerbation. Acute respiratory failure was questioned in the ED; on admission he was not in respiratory failure (SpO2 92% RA, normal work of breathing, reassuring ABG). Improved with steroids, bronchodilators and azithromycin. Room air throughout after the ED. Started varenicline.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: prednisone 40 mg x2 more days; varenicline starter pack; nicotine patch 21 mg; home inhalers (fluticasone/vilanterol, tiotropium, albuterol), amlodipine, atorvastatin, sertraline unchanged.
FOLLOW-UP: PCP 1 week; pulmonary rehab referral.

gold.explanation: The ED's 'acute hypoxic respiratory failure?' was a question, and the admitting physician explicitly ruled it out with exam and ABG; the discharge summary agrees, so no J96 code. Dyspnea, wheezing and sputum are integral to the COPD exacerbation and aren't coded. Secondaries carry no CC, giving DRG 192. A naive system that picks up 'acute hypoxic respiratory failure' from the ED note adds J96.01 (an MCC) and wrongly lands on DRG 190.
